verdict.rationale: LiteLLM documents performance-related proxy features—response caching to 'reduce latency' (litellm-docs-9/31), configurable worker processes (uvicorn/gunicorn/Granian) for scaling (litellm-docs-13/20), and traffic mirroring designed not to affect primary request latency (litellm-docs-39)—implying attention to gateway overhead, but there is no explicit benchmark or first-party/independent measurement of actual added latency (ms overhead) versus direct provider calls. Community threads mention flakiness/outages (litellm-comm-4) which is about reliability, not a concrete latency-overhead contradiction, so this doesn't rise to 'disputed'. Missing for 10: published latency benchmarks or independent overhead measurements, explicit statements about proxy hop cost in ms, and confirmation that caching/architecture choices translate into measurable minimal-overhead performance.
